vendor_api_version: Xero Accounting API 2.0 as served 2026-09-28, spec 19.0.0

divergences.route: GET /connections, GET /Connections and every authenticated route
divergences.reason: By default any non-empty bearer token is accepted. Xero refuses a token it did not issue with a 401 and www-authenticate Bearer error=invalid_token. strict_auth (the --strict-auth flag, or PUT /admin/config) restores Xero's behaviour.
divergences.operator_note: Added so a test suite that seeds a made-up token per test runs without registering one; strict_auth restores Xero's behaviour. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: By default a refresh token this emulator never issued is taken as a fresh sign-in and answered with a new token pair. Xero answers invalid_grant. A refresh token that was issued and already redeemed is refused either way, so single use holds. strict_auth restores Xero's behaviour.
divergences.operator_note: Same reason as the bearer divergence: a test suite seeds a made-up refresh token. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: A xero-tenant-id header is required, as on Xero, but by default an unknown tenant id is accepted and sees an empty tenant. Xero refuses a tenant the token cannot reach with a 403. strict_auth restores the 403. The 403 body itself is a guess at Xero's problem-details shape: the real one is not observed.
divergences.operator_note: Same reason as the bearer divergence: a test suite sends its own tenant id and expects it to be accepted. The default tenant id is that value, so its calls reach seeded data. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: A delivery that fails is retried a fixed number of times, at a fixed delay, by the kit's dispatcher, and then dropped. A subscription is never disabled and missed events are never held or replayed. Xero retries immediately, then every 15 minutes for up to 24 hours, then disables the subscription and replays held events for 31 days on re-enable.
divergences.operator_note: Scope exception granted by the operator on 2026-10-19: deferred. The first integration this emulator was built for uses no Xero webhooks.

divergences.route: outbound webhook deliveries: payload shape and intent to receive
divergences.reason: Details the research does not settle are guessed. Each delivery carries one event, with firstEventSequence equal to lastEventSequence. eventType is uppercase (CREATE, UPDATE). eventDateUtc has three fractional digits, as in the documented example. The intent-to-receive check sends four requests (signed, unsigned, signed, unsigned) and enables the subscription only if the receiver answers 2xx to the signed and 401 to the unsigned.
divergences.operator_note: Settling these needs a live delivery (quirk observe_via: traffic). Recorded as deferred.

divergences.reason: Only Contact.ContactID is read. Xero looks a contact up or creates one by name when no ContactID is sent, and updates the contact record from any other contact field sent in the document. Here an invoice with no ContactID, or an unknown one, is refused, and the other contact fields are ignored. An integration that sends a bare ContactID, because the second behaviour is why it reduces the contact to its id, is unaffected.
divergences.operator_note: Raised while building invoice create. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: TaxAmount on a line is the TaxAmount the client sent, or 0. Xero computes it from the tenant's tax rate for the line's TaxType, and tax rates (TaxRates) are not modelled, so no rate is applied and Total equals SubTotal unless TaxAmount is sent. TaxType values are accepted unvalidated.
divergences.operator_note: Raised while building invoice create. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: EnteredTotal and RoundingAmount (new in spec 19.0.0) are stored as sent and not used: Xero checks the computed total against EnteredTotal and applies RoundingAmount, which this build does not.
divergences.operator_note: Raised while building invoice create. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: A line with no UnitAmount and any DiscountRate or DiscountAmount is refused with a validation error. Xero's LineAmount is net of discount, so the gross cannot be recovered from LineAmount alone; what Xero does with this shape is unverified, so refusing is a guess.
divergences.operator_note: Raised while building invoice create. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: Only Status DELETED is read from a payment update; any other status is refused, and other updatable fields are ignored. A payment that is already DELETED or reconciled is refused, and an unknown payment is a 404. The wording of these refusals is a guess. The deleted payment stays in the tenant, and its invoice returns to AUTHORISED with the amount due restored; whether Xero keeps the deleted payment in the invoice's Payments is unverified, and here it is dropped.
divergences.operator_note: Raised while building payment delete. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: Only a payment against an invoice or a credit note is supported: a payment that names a Prepayment or Overpayment is refused with a ValidationException. Xero records these too; the plan does not cover them.
divergences.operator_note: A scope boundary of this release, not a decision about Xero. Tracked as deferred.

divergences.reason: BankAmount equals Amount and CurrencyRate is stored as sent, so a payment never converts between the invoice currency and the bank account's currency. Xero converts by the rate.
divergences.operator_note: A guess made where the research is silent; multi-currency payments are not modelled.

divergences.reason: By default an inline Allocation is accepted against an AUTHORISED or PAID invoice of the same contact and type, bounded only by the credit note's total: AmountCredited grows, AmountDue never goes below zero and a PAID invoice stays PAID. Both rules are guesses; the research has one example (part of an AUTHORISED credit note against an outstanding invoice) and does not say what Xero does with a PAID invoice or an amount above AmountDue. strict_auth (the --strict-auth flag, or PUT /admin/config) refuses an invoice that is not AUTHORISED and an amount above its AmountDue.
divergences.operator_note: Added for an integration whose refund flow allocates the whole refund to an invoice that is normally already PAID. Whether real Xero accepts that is unverified. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: By default a payment on a credit note is accepted when the credit note is AUTHORISED or already PAID and the payments on it add up to no more than its Total; the payment lowers RemainingCredit (never below zero) and the credit note becomes PAID at zero. Both rules are guesses; the research does not cover refund payments. strict_auth (the --strict-auth flag, or PUT /admin/config) requires an AUTHORISED credit note and an amount within RemainingCredit.
divergences.operator_note: Added for an integration whose refund flow allocates a credit note to an invoice in full and then pays the credit note's whole total as ARCREDITPAYMENT. Whether real Xero accepts that sequence is unverified. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: Xero has no health or reset endpoint. These two paths are control-plane aliases for GET /admin/health and POST /admin/reset, served so a consumer written for an earlier Xero emulator that used these paths can use this one unchanged. They are not Xero API, and no other control path of that emulator (such as /_xero/state) is aliased.
divergences.operator_note: Added for an integration whose Makefile waits on /_xero/health and whose test fixture posts /_xero/reset before each test. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: A contact that carries the ContactID of a stored contact is updated, with only the fields the body carries changed, and one with no ContactID is created by the rules of PUT /Contacts. Whether Xero also matches a Name that belongs to another contact is not settled by the research (reports disagree), so this emulator never does: such a Name is refused as PUT refuses it. A ContactID that matches nothing answers a 404 whose body is a guess. These rules are a guess until a sandbox observes them.
divergences.operator_note: Added so a consumer that creates by POST on the collection can use this emulator. Update-or-create by Name, which an earlier Xero emulator did, is deliberately not reproduced: it is not Xero behaviour (recorded as a known gap). Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: An invoice that carries the InvoiceID of a stored invoice is updated by the rules of POST /Invoices/{InvoiceID}, and one with no InvoiceID is created by the rules of PUT /Invoices. Whether Xero also matches on InvoiceNumber is not settled by the research, so this emulator does not: a number that belongs to another invoice is refused as PUT refuses it. An InvoiceID that matches nothing answers a 404 whose body is a guess and writes nothing. These rules are a guess until a sandbox observes them.
divergences.operator_note: Added so a consumer that creates invoices by POST on the collection can use this emulator. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: A credit note that carries the CreditNoteID of a stored one is updated, and one with no CreditNoteID is created by the rules of PUT /CreditNotes. An update is partial, may move the status DRAFT or SUBMITTED to AUTHORISED or DELETED, SUBMITTED back to DRAFT, and AUTHORISED to VOIDED, and the lines, totals and status of a credit note with credit applied or paid are fixed and it cannot be voided. An update may add Allocations, up to the credit remaining and by the rules of an inline allocation on PUT; one it already carries (a credit note read and sent back) is ignored. Whether Xero also matches on CreditNoteNumber, and every one of these update rules, are guesses: the research has no example of a credit note update. A CreditNoteID that matches nothing answers a 404 whose body is a guess and writes nothing.
divergences.operator_note: Added so a consumer that creates credit notes by POST on the collection can use this emulator. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: The order query parameter and the If-Modified-Since header are accepted and ignored: the default order applies and every record is returned, where Xero orders as asked and limits the list to records changed since the date. That is silent wrong data, not an error. Accounts also ignores where.
divergences.operator_note: Deferred: the first integration this emulator was built for passes neither order nor If-Modified-Since.

divergences.reason: The Idempotency-Key header is ignored, so a retried write creates a duplicate where Xero replays the cached response for a repeated key and answers 400 for the same key with a different request.
divergences.operator_note: Deferred and recorded. An integration that checks for a duplicate by lookup, not by header, is unaffected.

divergences.reason: summarizeErrors is not read on the contact routes: a contact array with an invalid item is refused as a whole, where Xero answers 200 with a per-item StatusAttributeString and ValidationErrors when summarizeErrors=false. Invoices and credit notes do read it.
divergences.operator_note: Deferred and recorded. An integration that creates one contact per call is unaffected.

divergences.route: Any path or method the emulator does not serve (another path version, another API family, an unregistered path, or a method a served path does not take)
divergences.reason: Authentication precedes routing, as on Xero: a call without a token the emulator accepts answers the 401 first. With one, the answer is a 404 (or 405 for a served path with another method) whose body is problem details with Title Not Found or Method Not Allowed. Xero's own body for an unknown path is not observed, so its words are a guess.
divergences.operator_note: Added after the first community audit of this emulator. Approved by the operator.

divergences.route: Any write whose body carries a value of the wrong type or a date that cannot be read
divergences.reason: The answer is a 400 ValidationException whose element names the field ("Name is not valid", "Date is not a valid date"). Xero's own wording for an unreadable value is not observed, so the message text is a guess. A body that is not JSON at all still answers a 400 problem with "The request body is not valid JSON".
divergences.operator_note: Added after the first community audit of this emulator. Approved by the operator.

divergences.reason: By default any client id, any client secret, any authorization code and any redirect URI is accepted, so a test needs no registered app. Xero checks the client and its secret, and redeems a code once for the client and redirect URI it was issued for. strict_auth restores those checks against clients registered with POST /admin/clients, and codes issued with POST /admin/authorization-codes, because the emulator has no developer portal and no consent screen. A refresh token is also bound to the client it was issued to under strict_auth.
divergences.operator_note: Added after the first community audit of this emulator. Approved by the operator.
